benchmark_kind: one-time cost of hiding per-owner data volume by pooling and shuffling pages
protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties. Threat model unchanged: any two of three servers may collude.
scope_warning: secure_shuffle measured at 1024 and 4096 rows of 2 columns on a single host. Federation-scale figures are EXTRAPOLATIONS using an n*log(n) permutation-network fit, roughly 50x beyond the largest measured point. The pooling mechanism itself is NOT implemented; this sizes it. Passive protocol only.
question: LEAKAGE_ABUSE.md ranks B_i, the per-owner page budget, as the highest-severity leak: it publishes each owner's data volume, readable off the input file length. The only implemented mitigation is uniform padding, which taxes a participant holding 1% of the largest owner's data at 100x its own weight. Owner-blind pooling would remove B_i entirely, but was recorded as needing a secure setup of unknown cost. This measures that cost.

fit.caveat: two points fitting a two-parameter shape; the exponent is assumed from the permutation-network structure, not established

headline: Under the declared 2-of-3 threat model the one-time shuffle costs LESS THAN A SINGLE QUERY. Hiding per-owner volume is therefore essentially free relative to serving the workload at all, and the padding alternative is strictly worse for every federation with unequal participants.

leakage_change_if_built.before: L includes B_1..B_n, one published volume bound per owner
leakage_change_if_built.after: L includes only the sum of B_i, the federation total

open_design_question.problem: Pooling changes where a key's pages live, so the directory descriptors that point at them must be updated to post-shuffle positions. The shuffle permutation must stay hidden from the servers, or the pooling achieves nothing, which rules out simply revealing it and rewriting pointers.
options: Tag each pooled page with its directory row and look it up by oblivious tag match instead of by pointer. Needs no pointer rewriting, but replaces a demux multiplication per page with an equality test per page, which the ORAM path-read measurement showed is far more expensive.
Apply the same secret shuffle to a parallel position array so pointers can be remapped in-circuit. Cheapest at query time; needs care that the remapping itself does not leak the permutation.

Have the owners agree on the slot assignment among themselves in a one-time setup. Zero MPC cost and no server-visible permutation, but the owners then learn each other's volumes, which conflicts with the problem statement's mutually distrusting parties.
open_design_question.status: unresolved; this is a design decision with a privacy/cost trade-off, not an implementation detail

what_this_does_not_show: Any implementation of pooling; only the shuffle primitive was measured.
The cost of the pointer-update step, which is the unresolved part.
Any real dataset, WAN, or multi-host result.
That the n*log(n) fit holds 50x beyond the measured range.
